clue.text: Annie, perhaps, spotted instrument played like a cello

blocks.note: Annie is an example of a stage musical, as the 'perhaps' signals
spotted means noticed or saw

explanation.surface: A performer in a production of Annie is seen with an instrument bowed like a cello.
explanation.walkthrough: Annie looks like a person's name, but here it stands for the show; 'perhaps' marks it as one example of a musical.
explanation.definitionFit: A musical saw is a handsaw bent and stroked with a bow, the way a cellist plays strings.

clue.text: Important chess piece capturing one

indicators.note: a chess piece capturing something takes it in, so one piece holds another inside it

blocks.note: any piece in chess or draughts can be called a man
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A key chess piece takes one of the opponent's pieces.
explanation.walkthrough: MAN holds I to make MAIN; 'Important chess piece' reads as one phrase but splits after 'Important'.
explanation.definitionFit: Main is a synonym of chief or principal, as in the main reason.

clue.text: Tell secrets — do so, nastily, to get even

indicators.note: doing something nastily twists it out of its proper shape, so the letters are scrambled

blocks.note: fifteen letters taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone advises spilling secrets spitefully as a way of taking revenge.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is a plausible piece of vengeful advice, and every letter of 'Tell secrets do so' is used.
explanation.definitionFit: To settle old scores is an idiom for taking revenge for past wrongs, which is getting even.

clue.text: Prevailing trend in Sri Lanka, one connected with tea

blocks.note: CL, from the old name Ceylon, is Sri Lanka's international vehicle registration code
the Roman numeral for one
maté is a South American herbal tea

explanation.surface: A report on the dominant fashion in Sri Lanka, linked to its tea trade.
explanation.walkthrough: Sri Lanka's tea suggests Ceylon tea, but the tea here is the South American maté.
explanation.definitionFit: Climate in its figurative sense is the general mood or prevailing attitude, as in the political climate.

clue.text: Servant's dismal day working

indicators.note: working as in being worked or kneaded into a new form, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: nine letters taken as written

explanation.surface: A servant grumbles about a gloomy day at work.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is short for 'is', joining the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A lady's maid is a female household servant who attends personally to the lady of the house.

clue.text: Fool crossing near very deep gorge

indicators.note: crossing here means straddling, so one word spans either side of the other

blocks.note: an ass is a foolish person
by means near, as in standing by the door

explanation.surface: An idiot clambers across close to a deep ravine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Near' as a preposition, not an adjective: by the river means near the river.
explanation.definitionFit: An abyss is a seemingly bottomless chasm, a synonym for an extremely deep gorge.

clue.text: Suppress geologist's first report

indicators.note: first points at the opening letter of the word it is attached to

blocks.note: to ban is to suppress or prohibit
the opening letter of geologist

explanation.surface: Someone buries a geologist's initial findings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Report' looks like the document being suppressed, but it is the definition, in the sense of a loud noise.
explanation.definitionFit: A report can be the sharp sound of an explosion or gunshot, which is a bang.

clue.text: A formidable opponent can cause one a difficult problem

blocks.note: first meaning: a person who is hard to beat or win over
second meaning: a puzzle that resists solution

explanation.surface: A tough rival can make life hard for you.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase applies both to a tough person and to a stubborn problem; the middle words just link them.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom compares something resistant to a nut whose shell will not break, used of people and of problems alike.

clue.text: Commando, new boy gripping end of knife

indicators.note: end of points at the final letter of the following word
gripping means holding tight, so one word clasps another inside it

blocks.note: green means inexperienced or new to something
a boy's name
the last letter of knife

explanation.surface: A commando and a new recruit holding the tip of a knife.
explanation.walkthrough: Green for new means inexperienced, as a green recruit is.
explanation.definitionFit: A Green Beret is a member of a commando unit, named after the headgear British commandos and US Special Forces wear.

clue.text: Dishonest fellow fired from amusement park

indicators.note: someone fired from a place is thrown out of it, so a letter is removed

blocks.note: F is the abbreviation for fellow
a funfair is a fairground with rides and stalls

explanation.surface: A crooked worker is sacked from the fairground.
explanation.walkthrough: Take the F off the front of FUNFAIR.
explanation.definitionFit: Unfair means not just or honest, so dishonest dealing is unfair dealing.

clue.text: Detain Danish gay, troublesome at the present time

indicators.note: something troublesome causes disorder, so the letters are thrown into a new order

blocks.note: fifteen letters taken as written

explanation.surface: A demand to lock up an awkward Dane, made in the present.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Troublesome' reads as describing the Dane, but it signals the shuffle of all three preceding words.
explanation.definitionFit: In this day and age is an idiom meaning nowadays, in the modern era.

clue.text: A learner driver seen on roads, whatever the circumstances

blocks.note: taken as written
L is the learner plate on a learner driver's car
ways are roads or routes

explanation.surface: A learner driver appears on the roads in all conditions.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a learner driver must show an L plate, hence L.
explanation.definitionFit: Always means at all times and in every case, so regardless of the situation.

clue.text: Treat popular deputy

blocks.note: to stand someone a drink is to treat them to it
in means fashionable or popular

explanation.surface: A well-liked second-in-command is given a treat.
explanation.walkthrough: Stand in the sense of paying for a round, as in 'I'll stand you a pint'.
explanation.definitionFit: A stand-in is a substitute who acts in place of another, as a deputy does.

clue.text: Disagreeable frau let gun off

indicators.note: going off means going wrong or awry, so the letters fall out of order

blocks.note: ten letters taken as written

explanation.surface: An unpleasant German woman fires a gun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Let off' looks like firing the gun, but 'off' alone signals the shuffle.
explanation.definitionFit: Ungrateful has an older sense of unpleasant or unwelcome, as in an ungrateful task.

clue.text: Hangman's halter quickly brought over head of evildoer

indicators.note: brought over means turned over, so the word is read back to front
head of points at the first letter of the following word

blocks.note: soon means without delay, quickly
the first letter of evildoer

explanation.surface: An executioner's rope is hurriedly brought over a criminal's head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brought over head' paints the rope going over a neck, but 'head of' belongs with evildoer.
explanation.definitionFit: A noose is the looped rope used by a hangman, a halter being a rope with a running loop.

clue.text: A 'rue' out to new French motorway

indicators.note: new suggests a fresh version, so the letters are made into a different arrangement

blocks.note: nine letters taken as written

explanation.surface: A French street leads out to a newly built motorway.
explanation.walkthrough: Rue is French for street, which supports the French setting while serving purely as letters.
explanation.definitionFit: An autoroute is the French word for a motorway or expressway in France.

clue.text: Religious leader, bishop, in rush to find cuddly toy

indicators.note: in places the preceding words inside the word that follows

blocks.note: Mary Baker Eddy founded the Christian Science church
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
to tear is to rush or dash

explanation.surface: A church leader and a bishop hurry off to look for a soft toy.
explanation.walkthrough: The religious leader is not a pope or archbishop but Mary Baker Eddy, founder of Christian Science; the pair go after the first letter of the rush word.
explanation.definitionFit: A teddy bear is a soft stuffed toy bear, the classic cuddly toy for children.

clue.text: Embarrassed, editor catching worker in the act

indicators.note: catching means holding, so the preceding words close round the next one

blocks.note: red in the face with embarrassment
ED is the standard abbreviation for editor
a hand is a manual worker, as in a farmhand

explanation.surface: An editor, blushing, catches an employee in the middle of misbehaving.
explanation.walkthrough: The worker sits between the two short pieces, the blushing colour and the editor.
explanation.definitionFit: Caught red-handed is an idiom for being caught while committing the offence.

clue.text: Take proceedings against one in part of London

indicators.note: in places the preceding item inside the word that follows

blocks.note: the Roman numeral for one
Acton is a district of west London

explanation.surface: Someone plans to sue a person who lives in a corner of London.
explanation.walkthrough: I goes inside ACTON. Action is used here as a verb, meaning to bring a legal action against someone.
explanation.definitionFit: To action a person is to sue them, bringing a lawsuit, which is taking legal proceedings.

clue.text: First in triathlon, Italian with the French name

indicators.note: first in points at the opening letter of the word that follows

blocks.note: the opening letter of triathlon
IT is short for Italian, as in Italian vermouth
le is French for the

explanation.surface: An Italian athlete finishes first in a triathlon alongside a Frenchman.
explanation.walkthrough: Gin and it is a drink of gin with Italian vermouth, which is why IT can stand for Italian.
explanation.definitionFit: A title is the name of a book, film or song, or a form of address.

clue.text: Lays into boy after short walk

indicators.note: after puts the word before it in second place, behind the one that follows

blocks.note: a turn is a short stroll, as in a turn round the garden
a son is a boy

explanation.surface: Someone attacks a lad after a brief stroll.
explanation.definitionFit: To turn on someone is to attack them suddenly, which is laying into them.

clue.text: Roman historian understood American

blocks.note: tacit means understood without being said
US is short for American

explanation.surface: A Roman historian is grasped by an American reader.
explanation.definitionFit: Tacitus was a historian of the Roman Empire, author of the Annals and the Histories.

clue.text: Feeling sorrow because of assassinated president

blocks.note: to feel sorrow is to be sad
at as in upset at the news, meaning because of it

explanation.surface: Someone mourns because of a murdered head of state.
explanation.walkthrough: Anwar Sadat, president of Egypt, was assassinated in 1981.
explanation.definitionFit: Anwar Sadat was the Egyptian president killed by gunmen during a military parade in 1981.

clue.text: Court jester, one about to enter royal house

indicators.note: to enter something is to go inside it, so these letters are put within another word

blocks.note: the Roman numeral for one
C is short for circa, about
the House of York was an English royal dynasty

explanation.surface: A palace fool, one of many, is about to come into a royal household.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About to enter' reads as 'soon to enter', but 'about' is C and 'to enter' is the insertion signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Yorick is the dead jester of the Danish court whose skull Hamlet holds.

clue.text: Forward, first to shoot on target

indicators.note: first to points at the opening letter of the word after it

blocks.note: the opening letter of shoot
an end is an aim or target, as in a means to an end

explanation.surface: A football forward is first to shoot at goal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Forward' looks like a footballer, but it is a verb, as in forwarding a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To forward a letter or email is to send it on to someone else.

clue.text: Words of exasperation used in desert about nourishment?

indicators.note: about means around, so one word is wrapped round the other

blocks.note: to desert someone is to forsake them
the goodness in food is its nutritional value

explanation.surface: Someone stranded in a desert swears impatiently about the lack of food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Desert' reads as the sandy noun, but it is the verb meaning abandon; the question mark flags goodness as food value rather than virtue.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a mild oath voicing impatience or annoyance, much like 'for heaven's sake'.

clue.text: Item-by-item record is kept by lieutenant

indicators.note: something kept by another is held inside it

blocks.note: LT is the abbreviation for lieutenant
taken as written

explanation.surface: An officer maintains a detailed inventory.
explanation.walkthrough: LT holds IS to give L-IS-T.
explanation.definitionFit: A list sets things down one entry after another, a record made item by item.

clue.text: Initially, Ken and Dan streak playfully, quite bare

indicators.note: initially points at the opening letter of the word it qualifies
done playfully means messed about with, so the letters are tossed into a new order

blocks.note: the opening letter of Ken
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Two lads strip off and run naked for a laugh.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Initially' seems to cover Ken and Dan both, but only Ken loses letters; Dan is used whole, with 'and' just joining them.
explanation.definitionFit: Stark-naked means completely nude, so wholly bare.
